title.value: Neural Networks as Paths through the Space of Representations
title.justification: The title is accurately extracted from the paper's details provided at the start, summarizing the focus on viewing neural networks' operations as paths through a representational space.
title.quote: NEURAL NETWORKS AS PATHS THROUGH THE SPACE OF REPRESENTATIONS Anonymous authors Paper under double-blind review

extractions.description: This paper explores the interpretation of deep neural networks as paths through a high-dimensional representational space, where each layer of the network contributes a step along this path toward a desired output. The study leverages recent advances in metric representational similarity, extending them with tools such as geodesics and angles to analyze and visualize the representation paths of different neural architectures, like ResNet and VGG, on datasets like CIFAR-10.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is focused on the theoretical and analytical aspects of neural network architectures and their representational paths, without addressing climate or ecological themes explicitly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: We put forward the spatial “path” analogy for deep neural networks, and quantitatively evaluate it using recently developed methods for representational distance.

primary_category.justification: The core theme of the paper revolves around neural network structures and representational geometry, with no direct reference to sustainable development or ecological applications.
primary_category.quote: Our work is motivated by a spatial analogy for information-processing: we imagine that outputs are “far” from inputs if the mapping between them is complex, or “close” if it is simple.

secondary_categories.justification: While the research discusses neural networks and metrics, it does not expand into areas relevant to ecological or climate-related sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: We develop a toolbox for analyzing geometric properties of sequences of neural network layers, and show how existing representational distance measures imply a rich set of geometric concepts beyond mere pairwise distance.

primary_sub_category.justification: The content does not align with any specific sub-category of climate or ecologically-related sustainable development goals.
primary_sub_category.quote: We are interested in using metrics between neural representations to explore how representations evolve spatially as they are transformed through the hidden layers of deep networks.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The research is domain-specific within the field of deep learning and representational analysis, not extending to sub-categories related to ecological or climate fields.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: This kind of orthogonality between layers has not been previously observed.

new_primary_category.justification: Given the research focus on neural networks and representational paths, no new sustainable development category is required as it fits current none relevancy for SD.
new_primary_category.quote: In our path framework, relatively narrow layers take shorter steps, and chaining them together increases the total achievable length, while wide layers are capable of taking a single large step.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The central focus remains within the analytic framework of neural network architectures and not on an area that necessitates a new sustainable development sub-category.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Figure 1 visualizes properties of the path taken by a well-trained Resnet-14 model, here we ask how properties of its path emerge over training.
